name: fairy battle

attributes.attribute: treated battle as rough risky play
their fairies contest like hurling teams
fairies fought night battles across them

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy battle is a folkloric motif. The fairies were seen as deathless, so warfare felt to them like a sporting game. It was a chance for rough and risky play. The fairies of the Irish provinces competed against each other much like hurling teams. They crossed the land to fight by night and brought their wounded home at dawn. A phlegm-like matter on early-morning bushes was read as fairy blood from these endless battles.

okr.objective: Fairy battle is a folkloric motif of sport-like combat among the immortal fairies.
key_results: Fairies were seen as deathless beings.
Their battles served as rough and risky sport.
Fairies of the Irish provinces fought like hurling teams.
Early-morning bush residue was read as fairy blood.
